				<r3d:description language="eng">The Maize Genetics and Genomics Database focuses on collecting data related to the crop plant and model organism Zea mays. The project's goals are to synthesize, display, and provide access to maize genomics and genetics data, prioritizing mutant and phenotype data and tools, structural and genetic map sets, and gene models. MaizeGDB also aims to make the Maize Newsletter available, and provide support services to the community of maize researchers.
MaizeGDB is working with the Schnable lab, the Panzea project, The Genome Reference Consortium, and iPlant Collaborative to create a plan for archiving, dessiminating, visualizing, and analyzing diversity data.
MMaizeGDB is short for Maize Genetics/Genomics Database. It is a USDA/ARS funded project to integrate the data found in MaizeDB and ZmDB into a single schema, develop an effective interface to access this data, and develop additional tools to make data analysis easier. 				<r3d:description language="eng">Through a unique combination of data management and scientific research, NSIDC enables scientists, educators, students, journalists and many others to better understand the cryosphere, why it’s important and how it’s changing. Key areas of NSIDC expertise include:

Stewardship and free distribution of scientific data from a broad range of sources including Earth-observing satellites, airborne remote sensing campaigns, field studies and historical observations.
Research studies of polar regions, the cryosphere and related climate processes.
Scientific analysis and insights on how regions of the cryosphere are changing, as well as educational content about what the cryosphere is and why it matters.
Creating software tools to access and work with data as well as providing robust user support to the NSIDC data user community.</r3d:description>

				<r3d:description language="eng">virus mentha archives evidence about viral interactions collected from different sources and presents these data in a complete and comprehensive way. Its data comes from manually curated protein-protein interaction databases that have adhered to the IMEx consortium. virus mentha is a resource that offers a series of tools to analyse selected proteins in the context of a network of interactions. Protein interaction databases archive protein-protein interaction (PPI) information from published articles. However, no database alone has sufficient literature coverage to offer a complete resource to investigate "the interactome".
virus mentha's approach generates every week a consistent interactome (graph). Most importantly, the procedure assigns to each interaction a reliability score that takes into account all the supporting evidence. virus mentha offers direct access to viral families such as: Orthomyxoviridae, Orthoretrovirinae and Herpesviridae plus, it offers the unique possibility of searching by host organism. The website and the graphical application are designed to make the data stored in virus mentha accessible and analysable to all users.virus mentha superseeds VirusMINT. The Source databases are: MINT, DIP, IntAct, MatrixDB, BioGRID.</r3d:description>

				<r3d:repositoryURL>https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ipd/imgt/hla/</r3d:repositoryURL>
					<r3d:repositoryIdentifier>10.25504/FAIRsharing.e28v7g</r3d:repositoryIdentifier>
					<r3d:repositoryIdentifier>SCR_002971</r3d:repositoryIdentifier>

				<r3d:description language="eng">The IPD-IMGT/HLA Database provides a specialist database for sequences of the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and includes the official sequences named by the WHO Nomenclature Committee For Factors of the HLA System. The IPD-IMGT/HLA Database is part of the international ImMunoGeneTics project (IMGT).
The database uses the 2010 naming convention for HLA alleles in all tools herein. To aid in the adoption of the new nomenclature, all search tools can be used with both the current and pre-2010 allele designations. The pre-2010 nomenclature designations are only used where older reports or outputs have been made available for download.</r3d:description>

				<r3d:description language="eng">NHLBI BioData Catalyst® (BDC) is a cloud-based ecosystem that offers researchers data, analytic tools, applications, and workflows in secure workspaces. It is a community where researchers can find, access, share, store, and analyze heart, lung, blood, and sleep data resources. And it is one of NHLBI’s data repositories, where researchers share scientific data from NHLBI-funded research so they and others can reproduce findings and reuse data to advance science. 				<r3d:repositoryURL>https://repository.dasch.swiss</r3d:repositoryURL>
					<r3d:repositoryIdentifier>10.25504/FAIRsharing.095469</r3d:repositoryIdentifier>
				<r3d:description language="eng">DaSCH is the trusted platform and partner for open research data in the Humanities.
DaSCH develops and operates a FAIR long-term repository and a generic virtual research environment for open research data in the humanities in Switzerland. We provide long-term direct access to the data, enable their continuous editing and allow for precise citation of single objects within a dataset. We ensure interoperability with tools used by the Humanities and Cultural Sciences communities and foster the use of standards. The development of our platform happens in close cooperation with these communities. We provide training and advice in the area of research data management, promote open data and the use of standards.
DaSCH is the coordinating institution and representative of Switzerland in the European Research Infrastructure Consortium ‘Digital Research Infrastructure for the Arts and Humanities’ (DARIAH ERIC). Within this mandate, we actively engage in community building within Switzerland and abroad.
DaSCH cooperates with national and international organizations and initiatives in order to provide services that are fit for purpose within the broader Swiss open research data landscape and that are coordinated with other institutions such as FORS.
We base our actions on the values reliability, flexibility, appreciation, curiosity, and persistence.
Furthermore, DARIAH’s activities in Switzerland are coordinated by DaSCH and DaSCH is acting as DARIAH-CH Coordination Office.</r3d:description>
					<r3d:repositoryContact>https://dasch.swiss/knowledge-hub</r3d:repositoryContact>
					<r3d:repositoryContact>info@dasch.swiss</r3d:repositoryContact>

				<r3d:description language="eng"><<<!!!<<<The data resource has been frozen and is no longer actively maintained>>>!!!>>> The Ligand-Gated Ion Channel database provides access to information about transmembrane proteins that exist under different conformations, with three primary subfamilies: the cys-loop superfamily, the ATP gated channels superfamily, and the glutamate activated cationic channels superfamily. The development of the Ligand-Gated Ion Channel database was started in 1994, as part of Le Novère's work on the phylogeny of those receptors' subunits. It grew into a serious data resource, that served the community at large. However, it is not actively maintained anymore. In addition, bioinformatics technology evolved a lot over the last two decades, so that scientists can now generate quickly customised databases from trustworthy primary data resources. Therefore, we decided to officialy freeze the data resource. The resource will not disappear, and all the information and links will stay there. But people should not consider it as an up-to-date trustable resource. For any new work, they should consider using alternative sources, such as UniProt, Ensembl, Protein Databank etc.</r3d:description>

				<r3d:description language="eng"><<<!!!<<< This repository is no longer available. >>>!!!>>>

NetPath is currently one of the largest open-source repository of human signaling pathways that is all set to become a community standard to meet the challenges in functional genomics and systems biology. Signaling networks are the key to deciphering many of the complex networks that govern the machinery inside the cell. Several signaling molecules play an important role in disease processes that are a direct result of their altered functioning and are now recognized as potential therapeutic targets. Understanding how to restore the proper functioning of these pathways that have become deregulated in disease, is needed for accelerating biomedical research. This resource is aimed at demystifying the biological pathways and highlights the key relationships and connections between them. Apart from this, pathways provide a way of reducing the dimensionality of high throughput data, by grouping thousands of genes, proteins and metabolites at functional level into just several hundreds of pathways for an experiment. Identifying the active pathways that differ between two conditions can have more explanatory power than just a simple list of differentially expressed genes and proteins.</r3d:description>

				<r3d:repositoryURL>https://armlifebank.am/</r3d:repositoryURL>
				<r3d:description language="eng">ArmLifeBank is a FAIR-compliant biomedical data platform developed to centralize, preserve, and share research data generated by Armenian scientific laboratories. The platform integrates genomic, transcriptomic, clinical, and multi-omics datasets into a unified and interoperable infrastructure, increasing the visibility, accessibility, and reuse potential of Armenian biomedical research.

Built on the FAIRDOM-SEEK framework, ArmLifeBank supports standardized metadata annotation, persistent identifiers, and ontology-based organization to ensure interoperability with international scientific resources. The platform provides secure data management, collaborative research tools, and analytical pipelines for reproducible data analysis. By consolidating research outputs from diverse biomedical fields, including population genetics, hereditary diseases, cancer genomics, environmental health, and plant genomics, ArmLifeBank promotes open science, strengthens international collaboration, and supports the development of precision medicine approaches tailored to the Armenian population.</r3d:description>

				<r3d:description language="eng">The Indian Crop Phenome Database (ICPD), a domain of the Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC) at the Regional Centre for Biotechnology, Faridabad, India, is developed for the sustainable archiving, management, and sharing of diverse crop phenome data generated across India. As a global agricultural powerhouse, India generates a significant portion of biological data, primarily from agricultural trials. However, much of this valuable data remains inaccessible, unpublished, and lost over time. ICPD addresses this gap by providing a user-friendly, centralized platform for freely archiving, organizing, analyzing, and sharing multi-crop phenome data in compliance with Minimum Information About a Plant Phenotyping Experiment (MIAPPE) and FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Re-usable) principles. Each dataset is assigned a unique, persistent IBDC accession. ICPD supports open and managed access submission modes. The database operates under a structured licensing framework (CC BY-NC-SA), ensuring proper attribution while encouraging ethical and non-commercial use of data.</r3d:description>

					<r3d:additionalName language="deu">Archiv "Deutsches Gedächtnis". Forschungsdatenzentrum des Instituts für Geschichte und Biographie</r3d:additionalName>
					<r3d:additionalName language="eng">‘German Memory’ Archive. Research Data Centre of the Institute for History and Biography</r3d:additionalName>
				<r3d:repositoryURL>https://deutsches-gedaechtnis.fernuni-hagen.de/de</r3d:repositoryURL>
				<r3d:description language="eng">The ‘Deutsches Gedächtnis’ archive is the research data centre of the Institute for History and Biography at the FernUniversität in Hagen. It archives all interviews conducted since the early 1980s as part of contemporary history research and documentation projects at the Institute for History and Biography. In addition, collections of interviews from third-party research are incorporated. The archive is constantly growing through the Institute’s own projects, the incorporation of older collections from third parties, and support for ongoing external projects.
The interviews are life-history, narrative interviews in the style of oral history. They were conducted as part of contemporary history research projects as well as projects in qualitative sociological biographical research. They relate to socio-political events in Germany or to German history. The interviews originate predominantly from within Germany, but also from abroad, and are mainly in German; one in five interviews is in another language.
The interviews are made available for research, teaching and education in the form of audio or video recordings, transcripts, minutes/memos and short biographies, as well as information on the context of the research. A large proportion of the interviews are accessible online following registration and login. Researchers can search using full-text search and filter options.</r3d:description>

The media stock of IWF Wissen und Medien gGmbH (1956 - 2011) was transferred to TIB in November 2012. This stock is not only made available for research in the TIB AV-Portal, but can also be used directly online, as far as possible, in the course of many years of measures for digitization, long-term archiving, indexing and rights clearance. 		<r3d:repositoryName language="por">NODC-PT</r3d:repositoryName>
					<r3d:additionalName language="eng">NODC-PT Metadata Catalog</r3d:additionalName>
					<r3d:additionalName language="eng">Portuguese National Oceanographic Data Centre</r3d:additionalName>
				<r3d:repositoryURL>https://data.nodc-portugal.pt/</r3d:repositoryURL>
				<r3d:description language="eng">The Portuguese National Oceanographic Data Centre (NODC-PT) is a spatial data infrastructure (SDI) dedicated to the management and dissemination of marine geospatial data. It is part of a global network of national oceanographic data centres coordinated by the International Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange (IODE) programme of the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC) of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).

The main objective of this infrastructure is to improve access to Portuguese marine data by promoting interoperable access to datasets that support scientific research and technical applications across several thematic domains, including atmospheric sciences, biological oceanography, chemical oceanography, marine geology, bathymetry, physical oceanography, environmental sciences, and administrative and reference data.

NODC-PT is jointly managed by the Hydrographic Institute (IH) and the Portuguese Institute for Sea and Atmosphere, I.P. (IPMA), in coordination with the Portuguese Committee for the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (CP-COI).

NODC-PT has been recognised as an endorsed action of the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (Ocean Decade), under Challenge 8: Create a Digital Representation of the Ocean.

Through this collaborative framework, NODC-PT facilitates the discovery, access, integration, and reuse of marine data, ensuring transparency and interoperability through the adoption of standardised metadata and international best practices.</r3d:description>
					<r3d:repositoryContact>centrodados@hidrografico.pt</r3d:repositoryContact>
							<r3d:type>disciplinary</r3d:type>
